docs.title: Methods — Modifying Value Types from Within Instance Methods

hints: Struct methods that change stored properties must be `mutating`.
`private(set)` lets anyone read `funds` but only the struct write it. Refuse withdrawals larger than the balance.
`guard amount <= funds else { return false }; funds -= amount; return true`.
jsBridge: `private(set) var funds` is a public getter with a private setter. JS would use `#funds` plus a getter. Struct methods that change properties must be `mutating`, because they replace the whole value.

compass.q: JS: `#funds` + `get funds()`. Swift: `private(set)`. Which is less code, and which is enforced at compile time vs runtime?
Struct `BankAccount` vs `class`/`actor`: if two screens share an account, which model is right?
Can a `mutating` method be called on a `let` constant? On an rvalue like `makeAccount().deposit(5)`?
Money in real apps: `Decimal`, cents, or a `Money` type with currency? Where does validation belong?
